title: Realization of strict birational laws over a Dedekind base
statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral domain such that, for every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Fields are allowed. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation with nonempty fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation here includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Products are fibre products over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Call an open $S$-dense if it is dense in each fibre over $S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo equality on an $S$-dense common open. An $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens.

Let $m:X\times_SX\dashrightarrow X$ be an associative $S$-rational law for which $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ are $S$-birational. Assume it is strict: there is an open $D$ in its domain such that these two maps restrict to open immersions $D\to X\times_SX$, and $D$ and both images are dense in every fibre of each projection $X\times_SX\to X$. Then there exist a smooth separated $S$-group scheme $H$ of finite presentation and an open immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow H$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $S$-dense image such that the multiplication on $H$ restricts to $m$ as an $S$-rational map. An $S$-group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams. For any two pairs $(H_1,i_1)$ and $(H_2,i_2)$ with these properties there is a unique $S$-group isomorphism $a:H_1\simeq H_2$ with $a\circ i_1=i_2$. No affineness, connectedness or reductivity assumption on the groups is imposed.

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Every non-generic point of $S$ is closed: a strict specialization between two nonzero primes would give a chain of length at least two below the larger prime, whereas its local ring is a DVR of dimension one. The local-ring dimension/generalization-chain formula rules this out. The affine scheme $S$ is Noetherian by its single affine chart and the hypothesis on $R$. Consequently a closed subset missing $\eta$ is finite, by the finite-closed-points lemma. This also covers the field case, when that subset is empty.

source.place: Conrad, Section 6.3, printed p.225, final paragraph; dimension and finite complement preliminaries

proof.text: Base change the strict law to $\eta$ using the strict-law base-change lemma. Apply the field case of strict-birational-law realization to obtain a smooth separated finite-type $K$-group $H_\eta$ and a fibrewise dense open immersion $i_\eta:X_\eta\hookrightarrow H_\eta$ realizing the law. The field is Noetherian, so these finite-type smooth separated objects are of finite presentation: smooth gives local finite presentation, finite type gives quasi-compactness, and separated gives quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Conrad, Section 6.3, printed p.225: solution over the generic point

proof.text: Use the inverse system $\operatorname{Spec}R_f$, $0\ne f\in R$, ordered by further localization. It is a small directed system of affine qcqs schemes, with affine transitions and limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$ (the colimit of these rings is $K$). By finite-presentation spreading, descend $H_\eta$, then its multiplication, inverse, identity, and $i_\eta$ with the fixed source $X$. Descend the finitely many associativity, unit and inverse equalities by part (3) of the same theorem, after descending the arrows by part (2); products are their base changes and finite-presentation objects. Obtain a group $H_V$ and $i_V:X_V\to H_V$ over one principal dense open $V$. Increase the index so that $H_V$ is smooth and separated and $i_V$ is an open immersion, by the three property-descent lemmas. Their qcqs hypotheses hold for finite-presentation objects over the affine stages. Their local finite-presentation hypotheses on arrows hold by the map-over-base lemma and qcqs permanence.

source.place: Tags 01YW/01YX, 01ZM, 0C0C, 01ZQ, 0EUU; spread the finite group diagram and the open chart

proof.text: Arrange that $i_V(X_V)$ is dense in every fibre by applying generic-open fibre density to this open in the finite-type scheme $H_V$ and shrinking $V$. Also spread compatibility with the law. The original strictness domain $D\subset X\times_SX$ is of finite presentation: the product is smooth and finite type over the Noetherian base, hence Noetherian, and every open immersion into it is quasi-compact; the other finiteness conditions follow from smoothness, from quasi-separatedness of the locally Noetherian scheme $D$, and qcqs permanence. Over $K$, the morphisms $i_\eta m_\eta$ and $\mu_\eta(i_\eta\times i_\eta)$ on $D_\eta$ agree on a dense open by realization. The smooth $K$-scheme $D_\eta$ is reduced; its dense open is schematically dense by the reduced-dense-image lemma, so separated-target uniqueness gives equality on all $D_\eta$. Part (3) of 01ZM now makes these two morphisms equal on all $D_V$ after shrinking $V$ again. Thus the fixed strictness domain itself witnesses rational compatibility over $V$.

source.place: Tags 054X, 01T6, 01ZM, 0EUU; spread the rational compatibility and its fibrewise dense witness

proof.text: Let $F=S\setminus V$; step 1 makes $F$ a finite set of closed points. For each $s\in F$, put $T_s=\operatorname{Spec}R_s$. It is the spectrum of a DVR by hypothesis. The base change of the given law to $T_s$ is strict by strict-law base change. The DVR case of realization gives $(H_s,i_s)$ over $T_s$, smooth separated of finite presentation by the same finiteness observation as in step 2. Both $(H_s)_K$ and $H_\eta$ solve the same strict law on $X_\eta$; uniqueness in the field case gives their unique group isomorphism identifying the two immersions of $X_\eta$.

source.place: Conrad, Section 6.3, printed p.225: local DVR solutions and comparison over the generic point

proof.text: For $s\in F$ choose a principal affine neighbourhood $W_s$ avoiding $F\setminus\{s\}$: for every other maximal ideal choose an element in it but outside the ideal of $s$ and take their product. Then $W_s\setminus\{s\}=W_s\cap V$ and the punctured local spectrum at $s$ is $\eta$ (a DVR has just its generic and closed points). Apply closed-point finite-presentation patching over the Noetherian affine $W_s$ to $H_V|_{W_s\cap V}$ and $H_s$, with the generic comparison of step 5. It produces a smooth separated finite-presentation $W_s$-scheme $\widetilde H_s$. The same equivalence is fully faithful on arrows: glue multiplication from the products, inverse from the group, and identity from the base, whose restrictions match on $\eta$. The group diagrams hold because the equivalence is faithful. Likewise glue $i_V$ and $i_s$ to an open immersion $\widetilde i_s:X_{W_s}\hookrightarrow\widetilde H_s$, using its open-immersion detection clause. Products have the required restrictions by base change. The patches of $X$ and of the base are their given restrictions, so full faithfulness identifies their glued objects with those objects.

source.place: Tags 0BPA and 0EY3; patch group operations and the chart by full faithfulness

proof.text: The image of $\widetilde i_s$ is fibrewise dense: all fibres away from $s$ are those over $V$, and its fibre at $s$ is the one supplied by $i_s$. To check rational compatibility without assuming any descent theorem for rational maps, compare the two everywhere-defined morphisms on $D_{W_s}$ given by $\widetilde i_s m$ and $\mu(\widetilde i_s\times\widetilde i_s)$. They agree on $D_{W_s\cap V}$ by step 4. The base $W_s$ is reduced locally Noetherian, and $D_{W_s}\to W_s$ is smooth (an open in the smooth product); smooth-reduced-dense-pullback therefore says that $D_{W_s}$ is reduced and that $D_{W_s\cap V}$ is dense. The dense open is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since $D_{W_s}$ is Noetherian. Reduced-dense-image schematicity makes its inclusion schematically dominant. Separated-target uniqueness gives equality on all $D_{W_s}$. This proves compatibility with $m$ on the original strictness domain, including the special fibre. The domain $D$ is $S$-dense in $X\times_SX$: for $t\in S$ and a nonempty open $O\subset X_t\times_{\kappa(t)}X_t$, pick $z\in O$ and let $x$ be its first projection; then $O$ meets the fibre of the first projection over $x$ in a nonempty open, which meets $D$ by strictness. Hence equality on $D$ is equality of $S$-rational maps.

source.place: Smooth reduction and density, reduced dense opens and separated-target uniqueness; the fixed original strictness domain suffices.

proof.text: Glue $H_V$ and the $\widetilde H_s$ along their specified identifications on $W_s\cap V$. For distinct $s,t$, the intersection $W_s\cap W_t$ is contained in $V$, so all comparison maps there factor through the same $H_V$ and satisfy the cocycle identity. Zariski gluing gives an $S$-scheme $H$ with these restrictions. Glue the multiplication, inverse, identity and the maps from $X$ by morphism gluing; their equations hold on the covering and hence globally. Smoothness holds by locality on the source after viewing each restriction as a smooth map to its open base and composing with that base open immersion. Separatedness and local finite presentation hold by target-open locality, and quasi-compactness by target-open locality of quasi-compactness; separatedness implies quasi-separatedness. Thus $H$ is smooth separated of finite presentation. The glued map $i:X\to H$ is an open immersion: it is injective, since two points with the same image lie over the same point of $S$, hence in one patch $X_W$ ($W=V$ or $W_s$), on which $i$ restricts to the injective open immersion into $H_W$; and every point lies in an open $X_W$ whose composite to $H$ is the open immersion $X_W\hookrightarrow H_W$ followed by the inclusion $H_W\subset H$. The local-on-source open-immersion criterion applies. Fibrewise density and rational compatibility are verified on those same base patches, using the fixed domain of step 7.

source.place: Conrad p.225 gluing; Stacks relative Zariski gluing and locality

proof.text: For two resulting pairs, the isomorphism $i_2i_1^{-1}$ between their fibrewise dense open charts is an $S$-birational map compatible with multiplication: use the common fibrewise dense domain where both realize $m$. Rational group-homomorphism extension therefore gives a unique $S$-group isomorphism $a:H_1\simeq H_2$ restricting to $i_2i_1^{-1}$ on the whole chart. This says $a i_1=i_2$, and the uniqueness clause of the same extension theorem is exactly the required uniqueness. It applies over arbitrary $S$, with no connectedness, reductivity, affineness or field assumption.
